fields.summary: Same-day appointments for pain
fields.body:
A toothache that keeps you up, pain when you bite, or a swelling that came on fast: call us before 10 am and we'll see you today.

We keep same-day slots at Oakfield every weekday. We take an X-ray, find the cause and get you out of pain first; the rest of the plan can wait until you are ready.

If the pain comes with a fever or a swelling that spreads to your eye or neck, call us straight away, or call 911 out of hours.

fields.bio:
Dr Reyes opened the Oakfield office in 2007 and still sees patients four days a week. She trained at Marquette and has a soft spot for nervous patients and complicated bites.

Outside the office she coaches her daughter's soccer team and grows far too many tomatoes.
fields.image_alt: Portrait of Hannah Reyes

fields.bio:
Dr Okafor places and restores implants at Oakfield and keeps the morning emergency slots. He joined the practice in 2012 after six years in hospital dentistry.

He explains every step before he starts, and stops whenever you ask.
fields.image_alt: Portrait of Samuel Okafor

fields.bio:
Dr Marsh looks after most of our younger patients and anyone who would rather not be at the dentist. She joined us in 2021 and leads the Pine Ridge office.

Slow visits, plain answers and a break whenever you need one.
fields.image_alt: Portrait of Lena Marsh

fields.bio: Priya has been our lead hygienist since 2014. Patients ask for her by name, mostly because she is the gentlest cleaner in the county.
fields.image_alt: Portrait of Priya Nair

fields.bio: Tom runs hygiene at Pine Ridge and is very good at talking small children through their first clean.
fields.image_alt: Portrait of Tom Alvarez

fields.bio: Megan runs both offices: appointments, insurance and anything that is not teeth. If you have a question about a bill, she is the one to call.
fields.image_alt: Portrait of Megan Shaw

entries.title: How often should you really have a cleaning?

fields.author: Dr Reyes
fields.standfirst: Twice a year suits most people. Here is who needs more, and who can wait.
fields.image_alt: How often should you really have a cleaning?
fields.body:
Twice a year suits most people. Here is who needs more, and who can wait.

Every mouth is different, so the honest answer starts with a look. At your next visit we will tell you what we see and how often we would like to see you.

What to do now

If anything hurts, bleeds or looks different, call us. Most questions take two minutes on the phone.
